item.intervention: Preparation of Si-20Cr-20Fe (wt.%) coating via fused slurry method
item.processing: Powders milled, mixed with 4% polyethylene alcohol binder, immersed, dried at 80°C, then vacuum oven at 1430°C for 1 h under 5 × 10⁻³ Pa
item.structure_change: Double-layer structure formed: outer high-silicon layer (MSi₂) and inner low-silicon layer (M₅Si₃); total thickness ~113 µm
item.attributed_mechanism: Silicidation and diffusion reactions occurred on the surface of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate; disilicide has the best stability due to enthalpy of formation
quotes: The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi 2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M 5 Si 3 as the inner layer.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: MoNbTaTiW Refractory High-Entropy Alloy (RHEA) substrate. Intervention: Preparation of Si-20Cr-20Fe (wt.%) coating via fused slurry method. Processing: Powders milled, mixed with 4% polyethylene alcohol binder, immersed, dried at 80°C, then vacuum oven at 1430°C for 1 h under 5 × 10⁻³ Pa. Test conditions: As-prepared state (before oxidation). Structure change: Double-layer structure formed: outer high-silicon layer (MSi₂) and inner low-silicon layer (M₅Si₃); total thickness ~113 µm. Mechanism: Silicidation and diffusion reactions occurred on the surface of the MoNbTaTiW RHEA substrate; disilicide has the best stability due to enthalpy of formation. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The initial silicide coating had a double-layer structure: a high silicon content layer mainly composed of MSi 2 as the outer layer and a low silicon content layer mainly contained M 5 Si 3 as the inner layer."

item.intervention: High-temperature oxidation at 1000°C for 1 hour in static atmosphere
item.processing: Heating rate 10°C/min, oxidation temperature 1000°C, time 1 h, static atmosphere
item.structure_change: Coating developed a three-layer structure: outer oxide layer (SiO₂, complex oxides) and inner silicide layer; oxide layer showed bulge and gap formation; silicide layer contained holes and cracks
item.attributed_mechanism: Swelling of the oxide layer caused by volume expansion during oxidation; pores in silicide layer resulted from diffusion of large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate
quotes: After oxidation at 1000 °C, the surface of the coating consisted of SiO 2 , TiO 2 , Cr 2 SiO 4 , Ta 0.3 W 0.7 O 2.85 , and Ti 0.67 Nb 1.33 O 4
The oxide layer exhibited a bulge phenomenon, and a gap appeared between the oxide and silicide layer after oxidation at 1000 °C.

The swelling of the oxide layer may have been caused by volume expansion during oxidation. The pores formed in the silicide layer were resulted from the diffusion of a large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Si-20Cr-20Fe coated MoNbTaTiW RHEA. Intervention: High-temperature oxidation at 1000°C for 1 hour in static atmosphere. Processing: Heating rate 10°C/min, oxidation temperature 1000°C, time 1 h, static atmosphere. Test conditions: 1000°C, 1 h, static air. Structure change: Coating developed a three-layer structure: outer oxide layer (SiO₂, complex oxides) and inner silicide layer; oxide layer showed bulge and gap formation; silicide layer contained holes and cracks. Mechanism: Swelling of the oxide layer caused by volume expansion during oxidation; pores in silicide layer resulted from diffusion of large number of silicon atoms into the RHEA substrate. Evidence: measured. Quote: "After oxidation at 1000 °C, the surface of the coating consisted of SiO 2 , TiO 2 , Cr 2 SiO 4 , Ta 0.3 W 0.7 O 2.85 , and Ti 0.67 Nb 1.33 O 4"

item.intervention: High-temperature oxidation at 1300°C for 1 hour in static atmosphere
item.processing: Heating rate 10°C/min, oxidation temperature 1300°C, time 1 h, static atmosphere
item.structure_change: Coating developed a four-layer structure: two oxide layers (L3 low-oxygen, L4 complete oxide) and two silicide layers (L1, L2); no gap between oxide and silicide layers; silicide layer had holes and cracks
item.attributed_mechanism: Complete oxidation of metal and silicon caused significant increase in oxide layer volume, while volatilization of some oxides (e.g., MoO₃) caused loss; volume of oxide layer became similar to initial silicide layer
quotes: After oxidation at 1300 °C, the surface coating was composed of CrNbO 4 , SiO 2 , WO 3 , and Fe 2 SiO 4

The complete oxidation of the metal and silicon could cause a significant increase in the oxide layer volume, whereas the volatilization of some oxides (such as MoO 3 ) could cause the loss of the oxide layer and reduce the volume

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Si-20Cr-20Fe coated MoNbTaTiW RHEA. Intervention: High-temperature oxidation at 1300°C for 1 hour in static atmosphere. Processing: Heating rate 10°C/min, oxidation temperature 1300°C, time 1 h, static atmosphere. Test conditions: 1300°C, 1 h, static air. Structure change: Coating developed a four-layer structure: two oxide layers (L3 low-oxygen, L4 complete oxide) and two silicide layers (L1, L2); no gap between oxide and silicide layers; silicide layer had holes and cracks. Mechanism: Complete oxidation of metal and silicon caused significant increase in oxide layer volume, while volatilization of some oxides (e.g., MoO₃) caused loss; volume of oxide layer became similar to initial silicide layer. Evidence: measured. Quote: "After oxidation at 1300 °C, the surface coating was composed of CrNbO 4 , SiO 2 , WO 3 , and Fe 2 SiO 4"

item.base_system: Initial silicide coating (MSi₂ outer, M₅Si₃ inner)
item.intervention: Silicon diffusion from coating to substrate during oxidation
item.structure_change: Silicide layer moved toward the inside of the substrate; thickness of high-silicon layer (L2) more than doubled (from ~67 µm to ~181 µm at 1000°C and ~194 µm at 1300°C)
item.attributed_mechanism: Silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred
quotes: Under high-temperature oxidation conditions, the silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred.
The siliconized layer moved toward the substrate.
During the oxidation process, silicon continued to diffuse into the substrate, and the thickness of the siliconized layer (L2) with a high silicon content are more than doubled.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Initial silicide coating (MSi₂ outer, M₅Si₃ inner). Intervention: Silicon diffusion from coating to substrate during oxidation. Processing: Oxidation at 1000°C and 1300°C. Test conditions: 1000°C and 1300°C, 1 h. Structure change: Silicide layer moved toward the inside of the substrate; thickness of high-silicon layer (L2) more than doubled (from ~67 µm to ~181 µm at 1000°C and ~194 µm at 1300°C). Mechanism: Silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred. Evidence: measured. Quote: "Under high-temperature oxidation conditions, the silicon element diffused from the silicide coating to the RHEA substrate while the oxidation of the coating occurred."

item.intervention: Comparison of oxide layer structure with 1300°C oxidation
item.structure_change: Oxide layer had a single-layer structure at 1000°C, whereas at 1300°C it developed a double-layer structure (L3 and L4)
item.attributed_mechanism: With increasing temperature, the degree of oxidation of metal elements was more complete and the oxide layer became thicker, and the oxide layer evaluated to a double-layer structure after oxidation at 1300 °C
quotes: The oxide layer had a single-layer structure at 1000 °C and a double-layer structure at 1300 °C.

With the increasing temperature, the degree of oxidation of metal elements was more complete and the oxide layer became thicker, and the oxide layer evaluated to a double-layer structure after oxidation at 1300 °C.
The structure and compositions of the oxide layer on the outer surface strongly depended on the oxidation temperature.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Silicide coating after oxidation at 1000°C. Intervention: Comparison of oxide layer structure with 1300°C oxidation. Processing: Oxidation at 1000°C vs 1300°C. Test conditions: 1000°C and 1300°C, 1 h. Structure change: Oxide layer had a single-layer structure at 1000°C, whereas at 1300°C it developed a double-layer structure (L3 and L4). Mechanism: With increasing temperature, the degree of oxidation of metal elements was more complete and the oxide layer became thicker, and the oxide layer evaluated to a double-layer structure after oxidation at 1300 °C. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The oxide layer had a single-layer structure at 1000 °C and a double-layer structure at 1300 °C."

item.structure_change: Total coating thickness increased from 347 µm (1000°C) to 397 µm (1300°C); oxide layer thickness increased from ~133 µm (L3 only) to ~169 µm (L3+L4)
item.attributed_mechanism: The coating oxidized at 1300 °C was thicker than the one oxidized at 1000 °C because of the higher diffusion rate of silicon, and the silicon had a deeper diffusion distance at the higher oxidation temperature
quotes: The thicknesses of the silicide coating oxidized at 1000 °C was 347 µm and that was about 397 µm after oxidation at 1300 °C, respectively.

The coating oxidized at 1300 °C was thicker than the one oxidized at 1000 °C because of the higher diffusion rate of silicon, and the silicon had a deeper diffusion distance at the higher oxidation temperature
After oxidation at 1300 °C, the average thickness of the oxide layer was ~169 µm, which the average thickness of the fully oxidized layer L4 was about 137 µm and that of the L3 layer was about 32 µm.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Silicide coating. Intervention: Oxidation at 1300°C vs 1000°C. Processing: Oxidation at 1000°C and 1300°C. Test conditions: 1000°C and 1300°C, 1 h.
